chunks: Abu Basir said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: O seeker of knowledge! Knowledge is possessed of many virtues. Its head is humility, its eye is freedom from envy, its ear is understanding, its tongue is truthfulness, its memory is investigation, its heart is good intention, its intellect is the recognition of things and matters, its hand is mercy, its foot is visiting the scholars, its aspiration is safety, its wisdom is piety, its resting place is salvation, its guide is well-being, its mount is loyalty, its weapon is gentleness of speech, its sword is contentment, its bow is diplomatic tact, its army is dialogue with scholars, its wealth is proper conduct, its treasure is abstaining from sins, its provision is good deeds, its water is cordiality, its indicator is divine guidance, and its companion is love for the righteous.

key_terms.الأخيار: Al-Akhyar — the righteous or chosen ones; in Shia context often refers to the Imams and their followers
key_terms.التواضع: Humility — the foundational virtue placed at the 'head' of knowledge
key_terms.المداراة: Mudara — diplomatic tact, gentle management of difficult people
key_terms.الورع: Wara' — scrupulous piety, careful avoidance of doubtful matters

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the virtues and attributes of knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), as transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to his companion Abu Basir, addresses those who seek knowledge with a rich extended metaphor. He personifies knowledge as a warrior equipped for a spiritual campaign, where each bodily part and military asset corresponds to a moral or intellectual virtue. This teaching was directed at students of religious knowledge in the early Islamic scholarly community, who would have understood the warrior imagery as a call to an interior jihad — the struggle against vice and ignorance — rather than outward warfare.
